header: Date: 2027-08-12 | Time: 14:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Hannah (Redwood CSM), Jared (Aurora Head ML), Priya (Security Lead), Liam (Platform), Sofia (DevOps)
summary: Weekly sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot with Aurora Robotics. Main topics: upgrade plan for runtime and node drivers, routing and LB config for cross-AZ traffic, KV/prefix cache tuning, SOC2/KMS questions, and next benchmarks. Agreed action items and timelines; Redwood to deliver upgrade playbook and security artifacts, Aurora to run a 24h throughput benchmark.
topics: Upgrade playbook and helm values for private deployment
Network routing and load balancer behaviour across AZs
KV cache / prefix caching tuning and effect on latency
Kernel/driver compatibility and planned node upgrades
Security: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML questions
transcript: 00:00 Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick checkin, well run 45 minutes. how are things on your side?
00:18 Jared (Aurora): Good, thanks. busy week but we got the new node pool spun up, had a small issue with driver mismatch so thats one reason we wanted to talk about the upgrade path.

00:33 Marco (Redwood SE): yeah we saw that in the logs you sent. looks like the NVIDIA driver on the older nodes is 525.x while our optimized kernels expect 535+. we'll walk through a non-disruptive upgrade plan.

00:48 Priya (Aurora): just flagging security side, we cant have an outage window longer than 15 minutes without SSO sessions dropping. also need to validate KMS integration before any key rotation tests.

01:05 Samira: understood. plan will include a canary rollout, pod draining and fast node replacement so sessions stay intact; well include guidance on kube-proxy & conntrack settings that sometimes cause slow reconnects.

02:02 Marco: on the runtime side, we recommend the 2-step upgrade: first upgrade drivers on a canary node, validate model serving with a smoke suite, then flip remaining nodes in waves. well provide helm values for nodeSelector and tolerations too.
03:15 Liam (Aurora): quick question on routing - in cross-AZ traffic we saw higher p95 latency when requests hit a pod in a different AZ. is that expected or do we need to change LB settings?

03:38 Marco: it can be both. LB cross-zone balancing plus Kubernetes service externalTrafficPolicy can cause source IP preservation tradeoffs. for low-latency SLOs we recommend local routing with sticky sessions for long-running KV cache warmups, and a fallback policy for cold starts.
04:10 Sofia (Aurora): were using GCP regional LB, currently cross-zone enabled. would changing that impact resilience?

04:25 Marco: theres a tradeoff: local routing reduces p95 but can reduce bin-packing and throughput slightly. we suggest a hybrid: prefer local, allow cross-zone for overflow, and set a routing weight that prefers nodes with warmed KV caches.
05:00 Priya: on encryption - Marco you mentioned KMS/HSM earlier. can you share the integration docs? we need audit log examples for our compliance team.

05:15 Marco: yes, Ill send the SOC2 artifacts and a KMS integration diagram after the call. note we support both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-managed keys; for HSM-backed keys we have an extra step during Helm install.
06:02 Samira: also adding that we can enable audit-log forwarding to your SIEM; well include example log formats. that was in the security pack we promised last week.

07:05 Jared: on benchmarking - we ran the small throughput run and saw about 650 tokens/sec per GPU with quantized LLM v1, but were not sure if caching config was optimal. we want to run a 24h throughput test to validate steady-state.

07:30 Marco: good call. often the first hour is warmup-heavy; KV prefix caching can significantly improve steady-state. Ill share recommended prefix sizes and TTLs. also watch for KV cache evictions when you scale down.
08:12 Sofia: noted. what about continuous batching parameters? we tried increasing batch windows but saw higher tail latency for small requests.

08:28 Marco: batching is workload-dependent. for chatty, low-token requests, lower batch windows help p95; for long generation, larger windows increase throughput but increase latency. we can provide workload-specific configs based on your prompt distribution.
09:45 Priya: security question: SSO/SAML - any gotchas for private control plane deployments?
10:00 Hannah (Redwood CSM): typically you need a line-of-sight for the control plane to your IdP or use a proxy. we have a pattern in the repo for SAML relay via a bastion if your IdP is on-prem.
11:12 Jared: about the driver mismatch - if we perform kernel or driver upgrades, what's the expected downtime per node?

11:30 Marco: with proper cordon/drain and node replacement we aim for sub-5 minute per node if you have spare capacity. the playbook will detail the exact kubectl sequence and preflight checks (GPU health, nvml).

12:05 Samira: ok lets talk rollback - if the new kernel creates perf regressions, we want an easy rollback. we recommend snapshotting helm release and having a node pool with old drivers ready as fallback.
13:00 Sofia: we'll reserve two nodes for fallback during the upgrade window. good to know.

14:20 Marco: small note on model kernels - some of our quantized kernels require specific CUDA minor versions; well list the compatible combos in the playbook so you dont hit weird FP32/INT8 fallbacks.
15:40 Jared: on routing again - any way to route by model size or metadata? e.g., send large context requests to beefier nodes?

16:00 Marco: yes, policy routing is supported. you can annotate routes based on model tag or request headers, and the control plane will prefer pre-sized node pools. we can show an example policy during the follow-up.
17:30 Priya: audit logs: how granular are they? do they include prompt hashes or raw prompts?

17:48 Marco: we include event-level records for request id, model version, token counts, and hashed prompt identifier by default; raw prompts can be included on request but that requires extra retention controls in your compliance settings.
19:02 Samira: well send a sample log with both hashed and raw examples so your team can vet retention policies.
21:20 Jared: quick UX note: we saw occasional 503s during scale events, might be kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion - any quick advice?

21:38 Marco: yes tune conntrack max and kube-proxy sync-period. well include recommended values; also enable graceful termination and preStop hooks to drain active KV cache items before pod exit if possible.
23:00 Sofia: preStop hooks could help but we need to ensure they dont block scale down too long. we'll test with a 30s grace window.

24:20 Marco: benchmark checklist: ensure single-model steady-state, run with and without prefix cache, measure p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU utilization, and end-to-end latency. we'll provide the spreadsheet template.
25:45 Priya: can you share the benchmark spreadsheet link now?
25:55 Marco: yes link will be in the follow-up: https://docs.redwood/benchmarks/aurora-pilot (placeholder link)
27:10 Jared: anything else on upgrades? were also curious about auto-scaling behavior for burst traffic - how does Redwood Dedicated differ from Private in that regard?

27:30 Hannah: Dedicated can give predictable throughput with reserved capacity; Private gives you control to autoscale based on node pool policies. for burst workloads you can configure a burst pool with pre-warmed nodes and a routing policy that falls back to hosted models if capacity is exhausted.
29:05 Priya: fallback to hosted model—does that send data outside our VPC? we need to confirm data residency and egress constraints.
29:22 Samira: by default Private keeps requests in your VPC; fallback to hosted is opt-in and we'd set strict filters—if you require no egress we can disable hosted fallback entirely.
31:00 Marco: quick note on metrics - enable token-level trace and model-level tracing during the benchmark so we can correlate cache hits to latency improvements.
32:40 Jared: agreed. well enable trace sampling at 10% for the run.
34:05 Sofia: anything about the upcoming minor runtime release thats relevant?
34:20 Marco: yes 1.12.3 includes improved KV eviction heuristics and a fix for memory fragmentation on long-lived sessions. we recommend it but will call out the kernel/CUDA combos you need.
35:50 Priya: any compliance changes in that release?
36:00 Marco: no compliance-breaking changes, just operational improvements, well highlight the audit log file paths and retention schema in the release notes.

38:10 Samira: recap: Marco sends playbook, KV cache recommendations, and benchmark sheet; Samira sends security pack; Jared runs 24h benchmark and posts results; follow-up next week to go over numbers.
39:02 Jared: sounds good. one last thing - can you include a quick checklist for a no-downtime driver upgrade? that would help PMs sign off.
39:18 Marco: yes checklist will be top-of-playbook - preflight, canary, smoke tests, rollback steps.
41:30 Hannah: ill send a calendar invite for the follow-up meeting week of 2027-08-23, please accept if that works.
42:05 Priya: thanks everyone. appreciate the clear next steps.
42:20 Samira: thanks all, well follow up with the notes and artifacts. bye.
42:30 [call ends]
